instruction:
Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Your task is to create a Verilog module that implements an arbitration block. 
An arbitration block is a type of digital circuit that resolves conflicts between multiple requests for a shared resource. 
The inputs to the circuit are the requests for the shared resource, and the outputs are the grants that indicate which request has been granted access to the shared resource.
Your module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: a set of n request signals (req1, req2, ..., reqn)
Outputs: a set of m grant signals (grant1, grant2, ..., grantm)
The module should also have the following parameter:

n: the number of request signals
m: the number of grant signals

Your module should implement the following functionality:

The circuit should grant access to the shared resource to one of the requests.
If multiple requests are active at the same time, the circuit should resolve the conflict by selecting one of the requests based on a predefined priority scheme.
The circuit should ensure that only one request is granted access to the shared resource at a time.

To implement the arbitration block, you should use Verilog code to define the priority scheme based on the input request signals. 
You should then use these signals to connect the inputs to the priority encoder and the priority encoder to the decoder.
Finally, you should use the decoder to compute the output signals.
